units.translation: which the scholiast explains: ἡ ψῆφος δὲ βαλεῖν τε καὶ ὀρθῶσαι οἶκον δύναται [the vote is able both to cast down and to set upright a house], so that βαλοῦσα [having cast down] is said for καταβαλοῦσα [having thrown down], on which see Thes. vol. 2 p. 87. Hermann refers βαλοῦσα [having cast down] to ψῆφον [the vote], since βαλὼν τὴν γνώμην εἰς ψηφιζόμενος [having cast his opinion into the voting] is understood: which could have been expressed more clearly by the passive βληθεῖσα [having been cast].
For thus it is correctly corrected in the apograph for μάθε [learn], which is in M.

It is a Doric form for βηλός [threshold], which the tragedians also used constantly in dialogue. Bekk. Anecd. p. 224, 15: τὸν τῆς θύρας οὐδὸν, ὃν Ὅμηρος βηλόν, οἱ δὲ τραγικοί βαλόν [the threshold of the door, which Homer calls βηλόν, but the tragedians βαλόν]. The grammarian of Hermann p. 444 adds the comic poets: βαλός: οὕτως ὁ βαθμὸς ἐν τῇ τραγῳδίᾳ καὶ ἐν τῇ κωμῳδίᾳ [βαλός: thus the step in tragedy and in comedy], whence Draco p. 35, 22 is to be supplemented, where L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 2 p. 95 noted that βαλός [threshold] has fallen out; βαλός [threshold] also in Hesychius.
